transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I'm just here because... well, it's probably nothing major, but my head has just felt a little foggy lately. I've been making these tiny mistakes in my client notes—I'm a personal care aide—and sometimes I just sort of forget what I was about to do. It's really not like me, I'm usually very on top of things. I just wanted to make sure everything is okay, if that makes sense?
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling in your head?

Um, I guess it's been... maybe about a month now? Give or take. It's just this sort of low... almost guilty, foggy feeling that's been hanging over me. I really thought I could just push through it and not bother anyone with it, you know? I know a month probably sounds like a long time to wait, and I'm sorry if I should have called sooner. I hope I didn't wait too long to come in. Is... is a month an okay amount of time to wait before getting something like this checked out?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you've had this foggy feeling?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm completely down *all* the time. I mean, I still go to work and talk to my clients and everything. I try really hard to keep a smile on for them, because they rely on me. But... yeah, I guess lately I've been waking up with this sort of... heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It's like I can get through my shift just fine, but inside I just feel kind of sad and flat. It's not so bad that I can't function, though! I'm still doing my job. I just... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. Does that make sense? Is it normal to feel like that sometimes?
Do you find yourself enjoying things you normally like to do, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family?

Well, um... I still try to do things. I don't want to let anyone down, so I still go to family dinners and, you know, watch the game with my brother when he asks. I guess... maybe I haven't been as excited about it as I usually am? Like, I'm there, and I'm participating, but it just feels a little more like going through the motions right now. But I still do it! I'm not, like, hiding in my room or anything. I just... maybe the spark isn't quite there right now. Is that... do you think that's just part of being tired from work? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um... weight? No, I don't think so. I haven't really been stepping on the scale or anything lately, but my scrubs still fit perfectly fine for work, so I think it's been pretty stable. I'm sorry, I probably should have checked my weight before I came in today, I just didn't even think about it. I hope it's okay that I don't have an exact number for you. Is... is it a good thing if it hasn't changed?
Do you feel guilty about things that you wouldn't normally feel guilty about?

Oh, um... well... I try really hard not to dwell on negative things, you know? But... I guess, lately, I've been having a little bit of a hard time with... well, my tío passed away. And I just... I keep replaying what I should have done for him before he died. Like, I really should have called him more, or made the time to visit sooner. I just end up feeling like I completely failed him as family. 

I know I shouldn't beat myself up too much, because I was working so many shifts and trying to be there for my clients, but... I don't know. Does that sound normal to you? I mean, everyone feels a little guilty when someone passes, right? I really hope I don't sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't find pleasure in them at all?

Um... no, not really. I mean, like I said before, maybe the spark is just a little dim right now, but I haven't completely stopped enjoying things! I still like watching the games, and I still love cooking for the family when I get the chance. I think it's just... you know, when you work a lot of hours as an aide, you just get a little worn out. But I definitely don't have anything that I just get *zero* pleasure from anymore. I try to stay positive and find the good in things, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Are there any activities that you used to find pleasurable but now find no pleasure in at all?

Oh, um... I think we might have just touched on that, right? I'm so sorry if my last answer wasn't clear enough, I probably rambled a bit. But yeah, like I was saying just a second ago, there really isn't anything that I get absolutely zero enjoyment out of now. I still like my usual things, you know, cooking for everyone and watching the games. I try really hard to keep a good attitude and stay active. Did you need me to go into more detail about my hobbies, or... was that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight recently?

Oh, um... no, I haven't lost any weight. I mean, my clothes all still fit exactly the same, so I think I'm holding steady! I try to make sure I'm eating enough to keep my energy up for my clients, you know? I hope that's a good thing. Is it okay that my weight hasn't changed?
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty about things that are not your fault?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard not to dwell on things, because I know it's not productive, but... sometimes my mind just goes there. Like with my tío... he passed away a while back, and I just... I keep replaying things in my head. Like, I should have called him more, or maybe I should have visited sooner before he got really bad. I just end up feeling like I really failed him, you know? Like I wasn't good enough family to him. But I know I shouldn't think like that! I was working so much, and I did what I could... I hope it's normal to feel a little regret like that? I'm trying to be better about letting it go, I promise.
Are there any activities that you have completely stopped doing because you no longer find any pleasure in them?

Oh, um... I think we might have just talked about this, right? I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. But no, I haven't completely stopped doing anything. I still do all my regular stuff, you know? I try to stay busy and keep up with my routines. I really hope that's okay! Did you want me to list out the things I do, or... was that answer alright?
Have you experienced any traumatic events recently, such as an accident, abuse, or a violent incident?

Oh, no, um... thankfully, no. Nothing like that at all. I haven't been in any accidents or, you know, anything violent. I try to keep my life pretty peaceful and safe. Especially with my work, I really need to be reliable and steady for the folks I take care of, so I try to avoid any kind of trouble or risky situations. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm just really glad I don't have anything scary to report there, if that's alright.
Have you had difficulty performing your job as a personal care aide due to your current emotional state?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I've had *difficulty*, exactly. I mean, I'm still showing up every day and doing my best for my clients, because they really depend on me, you know? I would never want to let them down. 

But, I guess... maybe just a little bit with the paperwork side of things? Like, I've been asking my coworkers to just double-check my client documentation for me. Just to be safe! I want to make sure everything is perfect. And, um, at home, my wife has been so sweet, she's taken over some of the bills and the scheduling stuff. I just... I haven't been quite as sharp with all those little details lately, so she's helping me out. 

Is that normal? I mean, everyone needs a little help sometimes, right? I'm really trying my best to stay on top of everything, I promise.
Are there any activities that you have completely lost interest in lately?

Oh, um, I think that's sort of like the first question you asked, right? About stopping things? I hope I'm not misunderstanding. But no, I haven't lost interest in anything. I'm still doing everything I normally do, and I still really enjoy it all! I try to keep a good attitude about everything, you know? 

I really hope I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I don't have anything like that to report? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you often feel guilty about things that you normally wouldn't feel guilty about?

Oh, um... guilty? Well, I mean, I wouldn't say I feel guilty about *everything*, or things I shouldn't feel bad about. I try to be a good person, you know? 

But, um... I guess lately I've just been... well, I keep thinking about my tío. He passed away recently, and... I don't know, I just keep replaying things in my head. Like, how I should have called him more often, or maybe I should have made the trip to visit him sooner before things got bad. I just... I end up feeling like I really failed him, as family, you know? Like I let him down. 

But I mean, that's probably a normal way to feel when someone passes, right? It's not crazy to wish you had done more. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is it okay that I feel that way?
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most things?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I've felt completely depressed or anything like that. I really try to stay positive! But, um... I guess this whole shift in how I've been feeling, with the paperwork and thinking so much about my tío... it really all started after he died. Which was, um, about two weeks ago. 

So it's been going on since then, but I'm really trying my best not to let it get me down too much. I mean, two weeks is a pretty normal amount of time to grieve, isn't it? I hope it's okay that I'm still feeling a little off since then. I'm doing everything I can to get back to normal, I promise.
How many days in a row have you been feeling this sad and flat?

Oh, um... well, I guess when I really think about it... it's probably been a little longer than just the two weeks since he passed. 

I mean, the really heavy stuff with my tío, that's recent, but... this sort of low, foggy feeling? Where I just feel guilty and kind of flat? That's actually been hanging over me for about a month now. 

I'm sorry, I should have been more clear before. I just didn't want to make it sound like I've been moping around forever, you know? I really do try to keep a smile on my face for everyone at work and everything. Is it okay that it's been going on for a month? I hope that doesn't mean I'm doing a bad job of handling things.
Have you had any significant changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

Oh, um... my sleep? Well, I mean, I always try to make sure I get enough rest so I can do a good job at work. Being a personal care aide, you know, people rely on me, so I can't be falling asleep on the job! 

But, um... I guess lately it has been a little bit... all over the place. Nothing too crazy, I promise! It's just... sometimes I lie there at night and I just can't stop thinking about my tío and all that family stuff. Or, um, sometimes I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just can't seem to settle back down and get back to sleep. 

But I mean, a lot of people have trouble sleeping when they have a lot on their minds, right? It's not like I'm staying up all night on purpose or anything. I'm really trying my best to stick to a good schedule. Is that... does that sound like a normal reaction to everything that's been going on?
Have you completely lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest in things. I mean, I still try to keep up with everything I'm supposed to do! 

I guess I haven't been doing as much of the fun stuff lately, like... well, I used to really like going out for walks or watching my favorite shows, and lately I just haven't had the energy for it. But I'm still doing my job and helping out where I can! I just... I think it's just because I've been so tired and distracted with everything. 

It doesn't mean I'll never like those things again, right? I'm sure once I get through this rough patch, I'll be right back to my old self. I'm really trying not to let it take over my life.
For how many days in a row have you been feeling sad and flat?

Oh, um... I think we talked about this a little bit earlier, but... I guess that sort of low, foggy feeling? The one where I just feel kind of guilty and flat? That's been hanging over me for about a month now. 

I really hope I didn't confuse you by saying two weeks earlier, I just... I didn't want to seem like I've been dragging my feet for too long. I really am trying my best to push through it and be positive, especially for my clients. A month isn't too terrible, is it? I mean, considering everything that's happened?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about significant changes in sleep patterns, which corresponds directly to the Sleep Disturbance symptom.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... my sleep? Well, I mean, I always try to make sure I get enough rest so I can do a good job at work. Being a personal care aide, you know, people rely on me, so I can't be falling asleep on the job! 

But, um... I guess lately it has been a little bit... all over the place. Nothing too crazy, I promise! It's just... sometimes I lie there at night and I just can't stop thinking about my tío and all that family stuff. Or, um, sometimes I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just can't seem to settle back down and get back to sleep. 

But I mean, a lot of people have trouble sleeping when they have a lot on their minds, right? It's not like I'm staying up all night on purpose or anything. I'm really trying my best to stick to a good schedule. Is that... does that sound like a normal reaction to everything that's been going on?

doctor.intent: determine the presence of marked diminished interest in activities
doctor.question: Have you completely lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest in things. I mean, I still try to keep up with everything I'm supposed to do! 

I guess I haven't been doing as much of the fun stuff lately, like... well, I used to really like going out for walks or watching my favorite shows, and lately I just haven't had the energy for it. But I'm still doing my job and helping out where I can! I just... I think it's just because I've been so tired and distracted with everything. 

It doesn't mean I'll never like those things again, right? I'm sure once I get through this rough patch, I'll be right back to my old self. I'm really trying not to let it take over my life.

doctor.intent: determine the duration of the patient's feelings of sadness and flatness
doctor.question: For how many days in a row have you been feeling sad and flat?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The low, guilty, foggy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of my sad and flat mood, which corresponds to the length of my depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... I think we talked about this a little bit earlier, but... I guess that sort of low, foggy feeling? The one where I just feel kind of guilty and flat? That's been hanging over me for about a month now. 

I really hope I didn't confuse you by saying two weeks earlier, I just... I didn't want to seem like I've been dragging my feet for too long. I really am trying my best to push through it and be positive, especially for my clients. A month isn't too terrible, is it? I mean, considering everything that's happened?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and feelings of guilt and worthlessness have been present for at least two weeks, meeting the diagnostic criteria for a Major Depressive Episode.
